samf-senior-2017-r1-02.title: Half the big circle
samf-senior-2017-r1-02.body:
Rotating the middle ring by $90^\circ$ shows that the shaded parts of each ring fill exactly half of it. So the shaded region is half of the largest circle: $\frac12\pi\cdot6^2=18\pi$.

**Answer: (D) $18\pi$**

samf-senior-2017-r1-02.title: Add the ring areas
samf-senior-2017-r1-02.body:
In each of the three regions (inner disc, middle ring, outer ring) two opposite quarters are shaded, i.e. half of its area: $\frac12\pi\cdot2^2+\frac12\pi(4^2-2^2)+\frac12\pi(6^2-4^2)=2\pi+6\pi+10\pi=18\pi$.

**Answer: (D) $18\pi$**

samf-senior-2017-r1-03.title: Add exponents
samf-senior-2017-r1-03.body:
$3^n\cdot3^3=3^{n+3}$, a perfect square exactly when $n+3$ is even. Among $-2,-1,0,1,2$ the odd values of $n$ are $-1$ and $1$; the smallest is $-1$ (check: $3^2=9$).

**Answer: (B) $-1$**

samf-senior-2017-r1-04.title: Read the graph
samf-senior-2017-r1-04.body:
The bars are $2$ (0-5 min), $7$ (6-10 min), $5$ (11-15 min) and $2$ (16-20 min). Longer than $10$ minutes: $5+2=7$ learners.

**Answer: (C) 7**

samf-senior-2017-r1-05.title: Equation of the line
samf-senior-2017-r1-05.body:
The gradient is $\frac{7-3}{4-2}=2$, so $y-3=2(x-2)$, i.e. $y=2x-1$. Only $(3;5)$ satisfies it.

**Answer: (A) $(3;5)$**

samf-senior-2017-r1-05.title: Midpoint
samf-senior-2017-r1-05.body:
$(3;5)$ is the midpoint of $(2;3)$ and $(4;7)$, so it lies on the line through them. The other options are not on the line $y=2x-1$.

**Answer: (A)**

samf-senior-2017-r1-06.title: Triangle inequality
samf-senior-2017-r1-06.body:
Let the sides be even integers $a<b<c$ with $c<a+b$. If $a=2$ then $c<b+2$, so $c=b+1$, which is odd: impossible. So $a\ge4$, $b\ge6$, $c\ge8$, and $4,6,8$ is a triangle ($4+6>8$). The minimum perimeter is $18$.

**Answer: (C) 18**

samf-senior-2017-r1-07.title: Shift by 3
samf-senior-2017-r1-07.body:
Each of the three largest numbers is $3$ more than the corresponding one of the three smallest, so $M=N+3\cdot3=N+9$.

**Answer: (B)**

samf-senior-2017-r1-08.title: Sign analysis
samf-senior-2017-r1-08.body:
The point lies on the line $x+y=2$. In the third quadrant $x<0$ and $y<0$, so $x+y<0\ne2$. The line passes through quadrants I (e.g. $(1;1)$), II ($(-1;3)$) and IV ($(3;-1)$).

**Answer: (C)**

samf-senior-2017-r1-09.title: Exterior angle theorem
samf-senior-2017-r1-09.body:
The marked angle $n$ is an exterior angle of both triangles: $n=a+b$ and $n=c+d$. So $a+b+c+d=2n$.

**Answer: (B) $2n$**

samf-senior-2017-r1-10.title: Favourable balls
samf-senior-2017-r1-10.body:
Neither red nor green means blue: $\frac7{8+7+6}=\frac7{21}=\frac13$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac13$**

samf-senior-2017-r1-11.title: Base and height
samf-senior-2017-r1-11.body:
The shaded triangle has its base along the side of the small square, of length $2$, and its apex at the top-left corner of the large square, whose perpendicular distance from that line is $6-2=4$ (the difference in the squares' sides). Area $=\frac12\cdot2\cdot4=4$.

**Answer: (E) 4**

samf-senior-2017-r1-12.title: Fill in a table
samf-senior-2017-r1-12.body:
Red shirts: $50-31=19$. Red with grey: $19-14=5$. Grey pants total $18$, so yellow with grey: $18-5=13$.

**Answer: (E) 13**

samf-senior-2017-r1-13.title: Two equations
samf-senior-2017-r1-13.body:
Let the container have mass $x$ and the contents when full $y$. Then $x+\frac y4=36$ and $x+\frac y3=40$. Subtracting: $\frac y{12}=4$, $y=48$, so $x=36-12=24$.

**Answer: (A) 24**

samf-senior-2017-r1-14.title: Equilateral triangle ADE
samf-senior-2017-r1-14.body:
$AD=BC=12$. In triangle $ADE$ the angles at $A$ and $D$ are $60^\circ$ (since $\angle BAE=\angle CDE=30^\circ$ and $\angle BAD=\angle CDA=90^\circ$), so $ADE$ is equilateral with side $12$ and $AE=ED=12$. The perimeter is $AB+BC+CD+DE+EA=12\cdot5=60$.

**Answer: (E) 60**

samf-senior-2017-r1-15.title: Eliminate a
samf-senior-2017-r1-15.body:
Subtract $3\times$(first) from the second: $-b-2c=-30$. Subtract $5\times$(first) from the third: $-2b-3c=-51$. So $b+2c=30$ and $2b+3c=51$. Subtract twice the first from the second: $-c=-9$, so $c=9$.

**Answer: (C) 9**

samf-senior-2017-r1-16.title: Trapezium
samf-senior-2017-r1-16.body:
Let $T$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $YH$ and $G$ the foot from $P$. Then $GT=PA=12$, $YG=18-12=6$, and $PG=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=8=AT$. Also $TH=\sqrt{17^2-8^2}=15$, so $YH=18+15=33$. Area $=\frac12(12+33)\cdot8=180$.

**Answer: (B) 180**

samf-senior-2017-r1-20.title: Spot the pattern
samf-senior-2017-r1-20.body:
The partial sums are $\frac13,\frac25,\frac37,\dots,\frac n{2n+1}$. With $50$ terms the sum is $\frac{50}{101}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{50}{101}$**
